newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Frenchman's mission to Mir postponed-Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Frenchman's mission to Mir postponed-Interfax.

text.p: Frenchman Leopold Eyharts will not be part of a relief crew due to fly to the troubled Mir space station in August, Interfax news agency quoted Russian space officials as saying on Monday.

It said space officials and designers had decided to drop Eyharts from a mission with Russians Anatoly Solovyov and Pavel Vinogradov, who are expected to carry out risky repairs required on Mir after a collision on June 25.
The agency said there would not be room for Eyharts because additional equipment had to be sent up to Mir to help with the repairs, the agency said.

The space officials and designers were meeting at Russia's Energiya company, a space rocket producer, near Mission Control at Korolyov outside Moscow. They were expected to decide who will do the repair work.
Vinogradov and Solovyov are due to blast off for Mir on August 5 and should reach the space station on August 7. They are already training for the repairs outside Moscow.

A cargo craft hit Mir during a docking manoeuvre on June 25 and holed a module attached to the station, damaging the power supply. The crew have suffered a series of mishaps since then, including a computer crash caused by human error last week.

Space officials have made clear they think Mir's crew -- Russians Vasily Tsibliyev and Alexander Lazutkin and British-born NASA physicist Michael Foale -- should not do the repairs but have not yet made a formal announcement on this.
